review_notes: I read the whole file. It introduces one new class, `IsKrasner K L`, plus the wrapper `IsKrasner.krasner` and two proofs that instances exist. I grepped Mathlib for "Krasner". The only hits were this file and `Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Dense.lean`, which imports it and uses `IsKrasner.krasner`. So Mathlib has no competing Krasner-style predicate or definition. `IsKrasner` packages the conclusion of Krasner's lemma as a Prop-valued class so it can be used as an instance hypothesis. It reuses existing notions: `IsSeparable`, `IsConjRoot`, `IsIntegral`, `Polynomial.Splits`, `minpoly` and `IntermediateField.adjoin`. The theorem `krasner` restates `krasner'` with `(minpoly K x).Separable` in place of `IsSeparable K x`. These are definitionally the same, so it is a thin named wrapper rather than a competing concept. I found no concrete cost that would justify consolidation.
